newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SIAULIU BANK HAS '96 PROFIT AFTER '95 LOSS.
newsitem.headline: SIAULIU BANK HAS '96 PROFIT AFTER '95 LOSS.

text.p: Lithuania's Siauliu Bank, one of the smallest bank's operating in the country, said on Tuesday that it had a net profit in 1996 of 3.9 million litas versus a loss of 2.9 million litas the previous year.

The bank's deputy chairman Donatas Savickas also told Reuters by telephone that the general sharholders' meeting on Monday decided to boost the bank's share capital by 14 million litas to 34 million litas.
He added that the bank decided not to pay dividends for 1996.
"The shareholders decided it was better to put two million litas into reserves and to use the rest of the profit to cover the losses of 1995," he said.
The bank said in a statement of audited results that its assets in 1996 rose to 70.674 million litas from 50.085 million litas.
Analysts say that the bank is a likely candidate for merger in 1997 as it scrambles to meet tighter central bank requirements.
